core_obligations: Assume I is maximal outside the family F and not prime, and note I is a proper ideal because R lies in F (proof lines 5426-5428).
Choose a, b outside I with ab in I; then both (I, a) and (I : a) strictly contain I, since the latter contains b (proof lines 5428-5430).
By maximality both ideals lie in F, and the Oka condition then forces I into F, a contradiction (proof lines 5431-5432).
proof_roadmap: Produce two strictly larger ideals from a failure of primality (proof lines 5425-5430).
Apply maximality to them and then the Oka condition to reach the contradiction (proof lines 5430-5433).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that a maximal element of the complement of an Oka family of ideals is prime (statement lines 5419-5423). The proof does not use prime avoidance or the nilradical: from a maximal non-member I that is not prime it produces two ideals strictly containing I, namely the ideal generated by I and a, and the ideal quotient I : a, which contains b outside I; maximality puts both in the family, and the Oka condition forces I itself in, a contradiction (proof lines 5425-5433). Finding exactly these two ideals is the content, and the author writes the double step out. H2.
